subject: math
skillName: Concavity and the Second Derivative Test
verificationNotes: Hand-authored; numeric answers checked with sympy.
intro: The second derivative $f''$ measures concavity. Where $f''(x)>0$ the graph is concave up (holds water); where $f''(x)<0$ it is concave down. An inflection point is where concavity changes, which requires $f''=0$ or undefined AND a sign change. The Second Derivative Test classifies a critical number $c$ (where $f'(c)=0$): if $f''(c)>0$ it is a local minimum, if $f''(c)<0$ a local maximum; if $f''(c)=0$ the test is inconclusive.

items.prompt: Find the intervals of concavity and inflection point of $f(x)=x^3-3x^2$.

steps: Concavity changes at $x=1$, so $(1,f(1))=(1,-2)$ is an inflection point.
solution.answer: Concave down on $(-\infty,1)$, up on $(1,\infty)$; inflection at $(1,-2)$.

items.prompt: Use the Second Derivative Test to classify the critical numbers of $f(x)=x^3-12x$.

solution.answer: Local max $16$ at $x=-2$, local min $-16$ at $x=2$.

items.prompt: Classify the critical number of $f(x)=x^4$ at $x=0$ using the Second Derivative Test, and explain.

steps: Fall back to the First Derivative Test: $f'$ goes $-\to+$ at $0$, so it is a local minimum.
solution.answer: Second Derivative Test inconclusive; First Derivative Test gives a local min at $x=0$.
